paragraphs.heading: What counts as renewable
paragraphs.text: Renewable energy, also called green energy, comes from natural resources that are replenished within a human timescale. It is usually understood as energy harnessed from natural phenomena that occur continuously. The International Energy Agency defines it as energy from natural processes that are replenished faster than they are consumed. To be renewable, an energy must be an endless source. Nuclear power is therefore not considered renewable, because it relies on non-renewable fuel.

paragraphs.heading: The main types
paragraphs.text: The main types are widely agreed to be solar power, wind power, biomass, hydroelectricity and geothermal energy. Some sources are variable, meaning they fluctuate, such as wind power and solar power. Others are controllable, including dammed hydroelectricity, bioenergy and geothermal power. Solar and wind, the two most important forms, are intermittent: they are not available constantly. Fossil fuel plants, nuclear plants and hydropower, by contrast, can usually produce precisely the amount of energy an electricity grid needs at a given time.

paragraphs.heading: Cheaper and growing
paragraphs.text: Renewable energy systems have rapidly become cheaper and more efficient over the past 40 years. In some places, the cheapest new-build electricity is photovoltaic solar or onshore wind. A large majority of the electricity capacity newly installed around the world is now renewable. From 2011 to 2021, the renewable share of global electricity supply rose from 20% to 28%. Most of that increase came from sun and wind, which together went from 2% to 10%. In 2025, renewables made up 34% of the electricity generated worldwide.

paragraphs.heading: Why switch
paragraphs.text: The main reason to choose renewable energy over fossil fuels is to cut the greenhouse gas emissions that cause climate change. In general, renewable sources also pollute much less than fossil fuels. They cause much less air pollution, which improves public health, and they are less noisy. Estimates put the potential savings in health care costs worldwide at trillions of dollars a year. Fossil fuels are concentrated in a limited number of countries, whereas renewable energy is spread more evenly across the world.

paragraphs.heading: Not the same as low-carbon
paragraphs.text: Renewable does not mean the same thing as low-carbon. Almost all forms of renewable energy cause far fewer carbon emissions than fossil fuels. But some non-renewable sources, such as nuclear power, generate almost no emissions, and some renewable sources can be very carbon-intensive, such as burning biomass when it is not offset by planting new plants. Sustainable energy is a different thing again: a more abstract idea that tries to group energy sources by their overall permanent impact on future generations. Biomass, for example, is often associated with unsustainable deforestation.

paragraphs.heading: How far there is to go
paragraphs.text: The International Energy Agency estimates that reaching net zero emissions by 2050 will need 90% of global electricity to come from renewables. The current pace of expansion remains far from that required rate globally. Obstacles remain, and the chief ones are subsidies for fossil fuels, lobbying by incumbent power providers, and local opposition to renewable installations using land. At the 2023 United Nations Climate Change Conference, roughly three in four of the world's countries set a goal: to triple renewable energy capacity by 2030.
